title: XI–XIII. Personal union; ineffable mode neither essential nor accidental
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): John 9:37). — 1 John 4:15; — John 20:31; — Since therefore there stands as one personality belonging toward both natures, there stands as also one person and one personal union (1 Corinthians 8:6; — but personal, by which in ye personality belonging toward ye Word as a common bond distinct natures, not inclining by any natural tendency to union, stand as gathered into one — a union whose like stands as not found in ye whole nature belonging toward things — against Eutyches confusing ye natures and Nestorius tearing them apart and wrongly dissolving ye unity belonging toward Christs person. — Although ye mode stands as ineffable, it stands as denied to be a conjunction or union that stands as either essential — by which things having a mutual and natural respect to one another stand as united, as act and potency, matter and form, genus and specific difference — or accidental, by which either accidents stand as joined to subjects or substances themselves stand as accidentally joined among themselves: — XIII. — In it stand as contemplated mode and effect. — XII. — Personal union stands as that by which ye Son belonging toward God joined ye assumed nature to Himself into ye unity belonging toward His person. — XI.
pass_b_english: XI. Personal union is that by which the Son of God joined the assumed nature to Himself into the unity of His person. XII. In it are contemplated mode and effect.

XIII. Although the mode is ineffable, it is denied to be a conjunction or union that is either essential — by which things having a mutual and natural respect to one another are united, as act and potency, matter and form, genus and specific difference — or accidental, by which either accidents are joined to subjects or substances themselves are accidentally joined among themselves: but personal, by which in the personality of the Word as a common bond distinct natures, not inclining by any natural tendency to union, are gathered into one — a union whose like is not found in the whole nature of things — against Eutyches confusing the natures and Nestorius tearing them apart and wrongly dissolving the unity of Christs person.
Since therefore there is one personality of both natures, there is also one person and one personal union (1 Corinthians 8:6; John 20:31; 1 John 4:15; John 9:37).
source_text: XI. Unio personalis est, qua Filius Dei naturam assumptam sibi in personae suae unitatem coniunxit. XII. In ea spectatur modus & effectus. XIII. Modus quamvis ineffabilis sit, tamen negatur esse coniunctionem sive unionem eamque neque essentialem, qua quae mutuum & naturalem respectum habent ad se invicem uniuntur, ut actus & potentia, materia & forma, genus & differentia specifica; neque accidentalem, qua vel subiectis accidentia, vel ipsa substantia inter se accidentaliter coniunguntur: sed personalem, qua in personalitate Verbi tanquam communi vinculo naturae distinctae, & nulla naturali inclinatione ad unionem propendentes, in unum colligantur, cuius unionis similis alia non invenitur in universa rerum natura — contra Eutychen naturas confundentem & Nestorium eas distrahentem & unitatem personae Christi perperam dissolventem. Quoniam igitur una utriusque naturae est personalitas, idcirco & una est persona & personalis unio, argumento 1 Cor. 8:6; Ioh. 20:31; 1 Ioh. 4:15; Ioh. 9:37.
